atoms.reason: Foundational, multi-proposal (A,C) decision: swapping the demonstrably-broken deep:deep_failed path for a proven FIND→VERIFY→SYNTHESIZE adversarial pattern is sound and high-impact. Low reversibility and high build cost dock simplicity, but the test is concrete and the bet de-risks the whole system.

Unanimous (A,B,C). Keeping the cheap nightly static guard separate from the expensive on-demand adversarial audit is the correct operational split and prevents the cron from accidentally triggering costly deep runs. Clean separation of concerns with a verifiable trigger contract.

penalties.reason: A fixed hard floor of 20 stated as absolute conflicts with COST_CONTROL_BUDGET_DEPTH (agent caps/token budgets) and with provider rate limits; floor should be a budget-and-rate-limit-bounded target, not unconditional.

atoms.reason: Refill-queue worker pool replacing a static maxParallelAgents cap is the right mechanism, but a non-negotiable floor of 20 fights both the budget profile and 429 reality. Modify: keep the pool and PID-verified target, but make the floor configurable and capped by budget/rate-limit headroom.

Live PID sampling with a peak_concurrency metric and timeline is the only credible way to prove the system isn't silently sequential — a known failure mode here. Highly specific and strong regression protection; impact is verification-layer rather than core function.

Restricting to Claude CLI + Codex CLI reuses the bridge's existing driver agent-invoke infra, avoids raw-API key management, and a two-provider split aids rate-limit failover. A constraint rather than a value-add, but a coherent and simplifying one.

Unanimous and essential: with 20+ concurrent CLI agents, 429/usage-limit handling with backoff and cross-provider rebalancing is the load-bearing resilience piece for the concurrency goal. Detecting limits from CLI output and rebalancing is non-trivial (lower feasibility/simplicity), but the failure mode is severe.

Reusing driver agent-invoke + lib/parallel.ps1 while explicitly choosing a read-only subprocess harness over the worktree/merge path is exactly right for a read-only audit. Strong specificity on what to fix (parallel-pipe, untracked-cleanup, codex hang) and how to test; feasibility/simplicity suffer because it touches known-unstable code.

Per-agent isolation so one timeout/crash/empty-reply can't abort a whole phase is mandatory for any 20+ agent fan-out; preserving stderr/artifacts and letting the orchestrator choose retry vs degraded quorum is the correct contract. High correctness and risk reduction at moderate cost.

penalties.reason: Tension with CONCURRENCY_FLOOR_20PLUS left unresolved at atom level — budget caps and a hard concurrency floor must be explicitly reconciled (budget bounds the floor).

atoms.reason: Unanimous governance: agent caps, token budgets, configurable depth, pre-flight estimate, and especially the VERIFY early-exit when FIND yields zero findings are the principled guardrails against runaway cost. This is the side of the resource-allocation conflict that should bound the concurrency floor.

Low-cost, high-reversibility process step that maps entrypoints, the deep-audit/deep-LLM layer, agent-invoke, lib/parallel.ps1, backlog writer, and scheduler hooks before coding. Cheap insurance against building the wrong thing given the high-cost/low-reversibility architecture atoms downstream.

A configurable dimension list with simultaneous finder launch is the natural shape of the FIND phase and the unit of parallelism that justifies the concurrency floor. Straightforward and testable; modest risk-reduction weight since it's a structural choice rather than a safety control.

An enumerated schema (root_cause, file, line, evidence_snippet, severity, why, fix_sketch, confidence) is required for downstream dedup/verify/synthesize to be machine-driven. Malformed-output handling (reject/repair) is the only feasibility wrinkle; very high specificity.

The adversarial core: false-by-default, simultaneous skeptics, majority-refute with mandatory file:line evidence, and retaining refuted findings for transparency. This is what turns a finder dump into a trustworthy report and is the main defense against false positives. High cost and complexity (many agents, voting) are inherent to the value it delivers.

Dedup, severity ranking, and idempotency-keyed auto-task creation close the audit loop into the existing backlog writer — directly addressing the recently-fixed 'findings never transition' gap. The idempotency key is the critical detail preventing duplicate-task spam across runs.

Single-proposal (B) but excellent and well-aligned with LLM_CLI_ONLY: passing dimension+location and letting the CLI read code (codex -s read-only, claude -p --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob --add-dir) avoids stdin context-stuffing, cuts tokens, and prevents stale-snapshot risk. Concrete flags given; it actually simplifies the orchestrator's plumbing.
